This position serves as the Greater Good Education (GGE) Program Director, overseeing the program’s mission to build kinder, happier schools where everyone belongs. This position leads the short- and long-term planning for GGE, shaping the program’s goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model. Working closely with the GGSC’s executive director, the Education Program Director manages fundraising for the program and ensures that the program’s direction aligns with the GGSC's overall direction. This position supervises a team that includes the Associate Director, Program Coordinator, Director of Learning Communities, Director of Educational Partnerships, Marketing Specialist, and Communications Specialist.
Lead Program Strategy and Development

The Education Program Director oversees all GGE program content, partnerships, and other activities, including training, evaluation, and communities of practice, while also overseeing the development of the new Greater Good Schools program, which focuses on integrating Greater Good values into the fabric of entire schools and districts. The successful candidate possesses extensive experience in K-12 education and a strong grasp of the science of social-emotional learning, mindfulness, character development, and other prosocial research in education. Additionally, this position requires an entrepreneurial spirit and a command of nonprofit strategy, development, and management.

Lead short- and long-term strategic planning for Greater Good Education (GGE), shaping the program’s goals, strategy, key activities, and funding model, in collaboration with the GGSC’s executive director and GGE program staff.
Identify and pursue funding opportunities for GGE, working in concert with the GGSC’s executive director, deputy director, and development director.

Write grant proposals to support GGE--in collaboration with the GGSC’s executive director, deputy director, and development director, along with the GGE team--and oversee the implementation and reporting on grants awarded to the program.
Lead the budgeting process for GGE and oversee the program coordinator's work, tracking program expenses.

Develop and maintain educational partnerships, helping to field-build and nurture a strong network of experts and practitioners. Oversee and collaborate with the Director of Educational Partnerships on new and ongoing partnerships.
Oversee and support the marketing and communications of GGE’s offerings by the marketing and communications specialists.
Contribute to short- and long-term strategic planning for the Greater Good Science Center as a whole, aligning GGE’s goals with the Center's.
Oversee Program Activities

Oversee the development of a new Greater Good Schools program as part of a two-year, grant-funded exploratory and design process, working closely with members of the GGE team who will be researching the opportunities, potential challenges, optimal model, and partners for the program.

In collaboration with the GGE team, synthesize the findings from this exploratory process in a final plan for Greater Good Schools that includes its program design, target audience, potential collaborators, marketing plan, financial model, and basic evaluation plan. Then lead fundraising and implementation for this plan.

Oversee and support the design, implementation, and evaluation of GGE’s activities that offer direct support to educators, including its Greater Good Educators program (led by the GGE Director of Learning Communities), quarterly “community meetings” (led by the GGE Associate Director), and partnership with California’s statewide CalHOPE Schools initiative.

Stay up to date on the latest research in prosocial education and oversee content creation for the Greater Good in Education website and the Education section of the Greater Good online magazine (in collaboration with Greater Good’s editors), ensuring that GGE meets its program goals and fulfills its commitments to funders and partners. Write or edit content as time permits.

Oversee the management of the Greater Good in Education website by the GGE program coordinator, providing input on the site’s design and development to ensure that they align with program goals and direction.

Manage the six-person education team, including supervising and supporting their day-to-day work, overseeing their schedules and priorities through regular check-ins, and completing performance reviews.
Attend weekly GGE team meetings and monthly GGSC staff meetings. Participate in discussions about GGE and GGSC operations and strategic direction.
Participate in monthly GGSC Directors’ meetings and the GGSC’s annual staff retreat.
Time permitting, attend and/or present keynotes/workshops at conferences.
Work with the GGE team on metrics for evaluating the program’s success. Oversee the collection, analysis, and reporting of program data, often working with an outside evaluator.
Advanced knowledge of the education field, especially the landscape of social-emotional learning, mindfulness, and/or character education, including research and best practices
Exceptional ability to make scientific research feel relevant, understandable, and inclusive to diverse, non-academic audiences, whether in written or oral communication
Exceptional organizational and project management skills
Excellent public speaking and facilitation skills
Exceptional writing skills, including for grant writing and reporting

Strong people management skills, including the ability to set a positive tone; recognize and provide opportunities for team members to use their strengths; demonstrate a positive work ethic with integrity; communicate with transparency and kindness; resolve conflicts in a timely and positive way; solve problems and make decisions with input from the team; and hold, communicate, and implement the vision of the program
